decisions.reason: Correctly walks resolve(): snapshot.current reads undefined on alpha.2, resolve() returns null at its first branch, onKeyDown exits before preventDefault so the chord falls through; explains both silences — all four guard probes still exist and undefined was the legitimate no-session state the code quietly ignores — without claiming the service or guard was removed.

Walks both session-controller excerpts showing SessionListState.current removed and navigation moved to view owners, and derives from the ui-session excerpt that uiSession.adapter.current yields a SessionBindingValue whose key replaces current and whose ctx replaces sessions.scope(id); maps to card DSH-0.1.6-A2-01 alongside the type walk.

Gives a concrete one-build resolve() that reads uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() with key/ctx on alpha.2 and falls back to the legacy current field plus sessions.scope(id), adds uiSession to inject, and routes binding.ctx through actx.get('conversation') and conversation.input.for(actx).

Correctly names the class — field-level removal behind service-member stability — and specifies value-level probes of 'current' and 'key' with a banner fallback. But the rubric requires noting the probe must run lazily or per-use, not only at activation, and the report argues the opposite, insisting on an activation-time probe and rejecting a lazy probe.

Verification covers mounting one dual-host build on both hosts, exercising chord behavior, session switching and the no-session null case, plus typechecking against alpha.2 published types. Prevention proposes a throwing deprecated current accessor naming the replacement, plus value-level guard re-probing, without claiming execution of the static fixture.
